newsitem.title: USA: Miss. shows tobacco can be pushed further-group.
newsitem.headline: Miss. shows tobacco can be pushed further-group.

text.p: Mississippi's $3 billion settlement with the tobacco industry suggested President Clinton and Congress should hold out for more concessions with the industry, an antismoking group said Thursday.
Action on Smoking and Health (ASH) said the Mississippi settlement showed just how far the industry could be pushed to make major concession.

"It suggests that other states whose trials are also coming up should hold out for large amounts to likewise compensate their taxpayers for money spent on Medicaid diseases, and that the President and Congress should not accept the 'deal' now being offered, but rather hold out for many more concessions," ASH said in a statement.

The office of Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore said earlier Thursday that the $3 billion pact would be superseded by last month's broader $368.5 billion settlement announced in Washington on June 20 if it was approved by Congress and the president.
